record.paper_title: Applying Saturation-Based Theorem Proving to Open Problems in Positive Implicational Logic
record.original_question: In positive (intuitionistic) implicational logic, with modus ponens as the only inference rule (from A and A -> B infer B), use the notation p(A) to mean that A is provable and i(A,B) to mean implication A -> B. Ulrich's fourth remaining 15-symbol candidate is the universally quantified formula p(i(i(i(X,Y),Z), i(i(Y,i(Z,U)), i(Y,U)))) for all X, Y, Z, and U. Is this formula a single axiom for positive implication? A negative answer would establish that the shortest single axioms for positive implication have length 17; an affirmative answer would produce a shorter single axiom.

evidence.quote: fof(u4,axiom, ![X,Y,Z,U]: p(i(i(i(X, Y), Z), i(i(Y, i(Z, U)), i(Y, U))))).
the question of u4’s status as a single axiom for positive implication remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider positive (intuitionistic) implicational propositional logic, whose only connective is the binary implication →. The only rule of inference is modus ponens: from A and A → B, infer B. A single formula φ(X₁,…,Xₙ) (with propositional variables X₁,…,Xₙ understood as universally quantified, so all substitution instances are available as axioms) is called a single axiom for positive implication if the set of theorems derivable from φ together with modus ponens (with uniform substitution) coincides with the set of theorems of positive implicational logic.

Define the formula
  φ := ((X → Y) → Z) → ((Y → (Z → U)) → (Y → U)),
in which X, Y, Z, U are propositional variables (implicitly universally quantified).

Question: Is φ a single axiom for positive implicational logic?

(An affirmative answer would yield a single axiom of length 15 symbols, shorter than the currently known shortest single axioms of length 17; a negative answer would establish that 17 is the minimum length of a single axiom for positive implication.)
artifact.status_search_result: Available sources indicate that, of the four remaining length-15 candidates for a single axiom for positive implicational logic, automated saturation-based theorem proving has refuted three by producing countermodels, but the status of the fourth candidate (the formula above) remains undetermined. No source found establishes either that it is a single axiom or that it fails to be one.
